reasons: The core blog design is essentially the same in both versions: rich dark gradient, elegant editorial serif typography, rounded cards, and clear category/search structure.

B feels cleaner and more premium because the assistant entry point is a restrained branded “Ask Fineguide” pill/icon, while A uses a generic chat bubble plus speech popup that looks more like a support widget and interrupts the editorial feel.
On phone, A’s chat message overlays important content in the Start here card and article hero area; B’s compact icon is much less intrusive and preserves the reading hierarchy.
Typography, article cards, navigation, filters, and overall findability are otherwise tied because the layouts and content presentation are nearly identical.

The underlying blog design is essentially the same, but A keeps the assistant entry subtle and integrated, while B shows a generic chat bubble that feels more like an intrusive support pop-up than premium editorial design.
B’s chat widget overlaps important content on both desktop and phone, including the hero image, start-here card, and article imagery, weakening hierarchy and making the page feel less polished.
A feels cleaner, calmer, and more mature because the floating assistant control is present without interrupting reading or browsing.
